title: SB5056 (2025-2026 Regular): Concerning Washington state patrol providing firearm background checks when state record systems are unavailable.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Washington); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Washington Legislature text (Introduced, https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/biennium/2025-26/Htm/Bills/Senate%20Bills/5056.htm, downloaded directly)
provenance.note: Introduced version. Sec. 1 strikes old (3) (hold on delivery under RCW 9.41.090 (4) and (5)) and an intent sentence in (4)(a). Sec. 2 renumbers later subsections.

operative_text:
Sec. 1 (RCW 43.43.580): (3) Notwithstanding subsection (2)(b)(i) through (iv) of this section, whenever a Washington state record system is inaccessible or unavailable in such a manner as to prevent the Washington state patrol background check program from complying with subsection (2)(b)(i) through (iv) of this section for a period of seven consecutive days, the Washington state patrol background check program may process the background check by complying with subsection (2)(c) of this section and conducting a check of:
Sec. 1 (RCW 43.43.580): (a) The national instant criminal background check system;
Sec. 1 (RCW 43.43.580): (b) Any relevant Washington state record systems that are available at the time of the background check; and
Sec. 2 (RCW 9.41.090): (3) Notwithstanding subsection (2) of this section, whenever a Washington state record system is inaccessible or unavailable in such a manner as to prevent the Washington state patrol background check program from conducting a background check for a period of seven consecutive days, the Washington state patrol background check program may process the background check by and conducting a check of: The national instant criminal background check system; any relevant Washington state record systems that are available at the time of the background check; and any other relevant agencies, databases, or resources as appropriate.
